paper.title: ChatGPT decreases idea diversity in brainstorming

paper.version_read: Published journal version of record, Nature Human Behaviour, Volume 9, June 2025, pp. 1107–1109; Matters arising; DOI 10.1038/s41562-025-02173-x; published online 14 May 2025. The local PDF includes the article and appended Nature Portfolio Reporting Summary.
paper.one_line_finding: In a reanalysis of Lee and Chung's (2024) experiments, ChatGPT-aided idea pools had a lower fraction of unique ideas (Universal Sentence Encoder cosine threshold 0.8) than comparison pools in every experiment, for example 0.74 vs 0.96 with web search (Experiment 1), 0.70 vs 0.92 unaided and 0.91 with web search (Experiment 2a), and 0.41 vs 1.00 unaided (Experiment 2b); the paper reports the difference as significant in four of five experiments, all but Experiment 4 (p. 1108, Fig. 1 and text).

estimates.notes: The whole randomized arm pools are compared on diversity across people, with AI available while the assisted outputs were produced; question=across_people, construct=diversity, unit=set, outcome_with_ai=true and within_person=null were independently checked. Higher unique-concept values mean more diversity. The reanalysis says each participant submitted one idea (PDF p. 1, printed p. 1107), but the original Experiment 1 allowed multiple ideas in one text response (c010 PDF p. 6, printed p. 1911). Arm levels are recorded in percent exactly as the table prints them; RD and its confidence interval are recorded in proportions, not percentage points. No unit conversion, difference, standard deviation or standard error was calculated. The reported standardized effect is Cohen's h, stored with paper_effect.type=other. Tests are two-sided and the supplement legend describes the p-values as Bonferroni corrected within each experiment. The main Fig. 1 caption calls difference confidence intervals Bonferroni-corrected, whereas the supplement legend specifies correction for p-values only. The printed intervals and p-values are retained without adjustment; the interval correction status remains unresolved. The stored confidence interval now describes the printed RD contrast; arm-specific interval endpoints are not printed. Study 1 uses one complete submission embedding per participant, verified against the local author notebook and its input CSVs (see supplement_fixes for source locations). Both input pools match the cleaned participant file's idea_text_raw submissions one-to-one within their assigned arms after whitespace normalization and correction of two character-encoding artifacts. The proportions z-test uses the whole participant submissions as its denominators. Under extraction-spec.md, one analyzed output per randomized person has se_basis=participant; participants who supplied several ideas still enter once. No preregistration or preregistered primary test for this secondary diversity analysis is stated in the supplement.
